blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Signs Your McHenry Main Line Needs Rodding
blocks.intro: One slow sink isn't the main. These are:

tiles.h3: Water Rising at the Floor Drain
tiles.body: Most McHenry basements have a floor drain at the lowest point. A main line clog shows up there first.
Air pushing back up through other fixtures when water runs means the line ahead is blocked.
Kitchen, bath and laundry slowing at the same time point to one shared line.
Standing wastewater in a blocked line can push odor back through drains.

blocks.h2: What Blocks Main Lines in McHenry
blocks.intro: With most homes built since 1970, McHenry clogs come more often from what goes down the drain and how the line was laid than from century-old pipe.

items.body: A low spot in the line holds water and paper. Rodding opens it, but it tends to come back until the sag is fixed.
Flushable wipes and kitchen grease build into plugs in otherwise healthy lines.
In homes from the 1970s and 1980s, roots from maturing trees find joints and grow into mats.
Buildup on the walls calls for [hydro jetting](/mchenry/hydro-jetting). A sag or crack on camera calls for a [sewer repair](/mchenry/sewer-repair).

blocks.intro: Clear it, then show you why it happened.

steps.body: We find the cleanout and work from there so the house stays clean.
We clear the line to the main, then camera it so you see the cause.
If there's damage, you get options and a price for each.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: How often should my main line be rodded?
items.preview: Only as often as your line needs. The camera tells us.
items.answer: It depends on the cause. Lines with roots usually need yearly service. Lines that clogged from wipes or grease may not need regular rodding at all. A camera look after the first clearing tells us.

items.q: Why does my line keep clogging in the same place?
items.preview: Usually a sag or a root-filled joint at that spot.
items.answer: When clogs keep forming at the same distance from the house, there's usually a sag or a damaged joint there. The camera shows it, and fixing that one spot often ends the problem.

items.q: Is rodding safe for my pipes?
items.preview: Yes, with the right head and a camera check.
items.answer: Yes. We choose a cutting head sized to your pipe and check the line on camera afterward.

items.q: Can you rod a line if my house is on septic?
items.preview: Yes, between the house and the tank.
items.answer: Yes. Some homes outside city sewer in McHenry County drain to a septic tank. We can clear the line between the house and the tank, and we'll tell you if the problem is the tank itself.

items.q: How much does sewer rodding cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on access and the blockage. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access to the cleanout, the length of the line and what's blocking it. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
